clue.text: Poor on the rink, perhaps, needing special intervention

definitions.meaning: a skater who is poor on the rink might be described as ..., decent only when away from the frozen surface
mediation or help offered by someone with influence

explanation.surface: A clumsy skater needs some special help to stay upright on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as GOOD OFF ICES: someone who only shines away from the ice is poor on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for mediation or assistance offered by an influential party.

clue.text: Rule extracted from original idea provides beautiful example

indicators.note: extracted from says one letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: the germ of an idea is its first seed

explanation.surface: Pulling a rule out of a first idea yields a lovely case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' takes R out of GERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a person or thing that is an outstanding, admirable instance of its kind.

clue.text: Irish golfing dynasty against participating in US award, heading off

indicators.note: participating in puts one piece inside the other, taking part within it
heading off means the first letter of the award word is dropped

parts.note: honor is the American spelling of an honour or award
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An Irish family of golfers opposes taking part in some American prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' and 'participating in' are the indicators; the award uses the American spelling. Christy O'Connor senior and junior were famous Irish professional golfers.
explanation.definitionFit: The O'Connor family, uncle and nephew both named Christy, were leading Irish professional golfers.

clue.text: Last character in repechage, mostly upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rowing repechage mostly ends with an upset for the final competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no word for the hidden step; 'in' is that signal. 'upset' reverses AGEMO, found inside 'repechage, mostly', in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last character.

clue.text: Fellow to come to earth — after this?

definitions.text: Fellow to come to earth — after this?

parts.note: to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A man is due to land again, presumably after some airborne trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: after a trip through the air, a person comes back down to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey by air is what precedes landing, so coming down to earth follows it.

clue.text: Name rich working business leaders

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Wealthy, busy executives make a name for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges NAMERICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who preside over company boards are top figures in commerce.

clue.text: Restricted by winter, the start of summer, and now spring

indicators.note: the start of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: Seasons are listed, from winter through summer to spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a season alongside winter and summer, but it is the verb to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off by heavy drifts is being confined by the cold season's weather.

clue.text: Bluebottle caught with a little work

definitions.note: old British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an op is a short musical work, from opus

explanation.surface: A blowfly is trapped with only a small task done.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebottle is old British slang for a police officer, not just the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated slang term for a uniformed police officer, matching the slang term for a constable.

clue.text: Church outbuilding unfinished, overlooking lake and stream

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the earlier piece above the next
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an annex is an extra building attached to a main one

explanation.surface: An incomplete church extension looks over a lake and a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts ANNEX to ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercourse or narrow body of water is a synonym for a stream.

clue.text: Attractive girl, keen on sex, seizing Bishop's drink

parts.note: a peach is an old-fashioned word for a lovely young woman
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy is British slang for lustful

explanation.surface: A lustful beauty grabs a clergyman's glass of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts B inside RANDY to make BRANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fruit liqueur or spirit, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Runs from bad-tempered deer

indicators.note: from here means the letter goes away from the longer word

parts.note: morose means sullen or gloomy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A deer flees an irritable animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes R out of MOROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest member of the cervid family, known in Europe as the elk.

clue.text: The girl one loves, independent and repulsed at a city-dweller in Italy

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the words are turned round

parts.note: a Roman lives in Italy's capital

explanation.surface: A freethinking woman is put off by someone from an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' reverses AT A ROMAN to NAMORATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a female sweetheart or beloved woman.

clue.text: Burns with heat, possibly? One does

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters may form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person burns in the heat and gets the reply that one does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BURNSHEAT. The definition 'One does' leans on the clue's opening: one who lies in the sun does burn with heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in strong sunshine is the person who burns with heat.

clue.text: Something attempted by those who are crackers?

definitions.text: Something attempted by those who are crackers?

parts.words: Something attempted by those who are crackers?
parts.note: crackers seems to mean mad people, but here means thieves who crack open strongrooms

explanation.surface: Seemingly a reckless stunt tried by lunatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like slang for crazy, but means safecrackers, who may use explosives on a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into a strongbox with explosives is what professional safecrackers do.

clue.text: Magistrates quail, sending 50 down

indicators.note: sending with down says a letter is dispatched away from the word
down with sending means the letter is removed, sent down

parts.note: to quail or blench is to flinch in fear
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The court officials flinch, convicting fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending ... down' takes L out of BLENCH. 'sending down' suggests prison sentences from the court.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench collectively means the judges or justices sitting in court.

clue.text: Providing backing to cartel leads to dismissal

indicators.note: backing means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: if means providing that
a ring is a group of traders fixing prices

explanation.surface: Supporting the bosses of a cartel gets someone sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses IF to FI. 'Providing backing' looks like giving support, and 'cartel leads' like its bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked from a job is being let go or discharged.

clue.text: Also known as fellow turning up in hot surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the stolen word encloses the other piece

parts.note: hot goods are stolen, or nicked in British slang

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man appears in a hot setting, under an alias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' and 'surroundings' are the indicators; 'hot' means stolen, which British slang calls nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called by an informal alternative name is going by another title.

clue.text: Endless remorse, tucking into booze? Charming fellow!

indicators.note: tucking into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: beer is alcoholic drink

indicators.note: Endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: guilt is a feeling of remorse

explanation.surface: Ceaseless regret sends a man into drink, yet he is still delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' and 'tucking into' are the indicators; the surface's charming fellow is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who enchants or seduces with wiles is one who charms.

clue.text: Guns and rifles initially piled up, brought in formerly

indicators.note: brought in says the reversed letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: piled up in a down clue means stacked from bottom to top, so reversed
initially means the opening letter only

explanation.surface: Weapons and firearms were stacked up and brought indoors long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' reverses ANDR to RDNA; 'brought in' sets it inside ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery and military weapons collectively, the heavy guns of an army.

clue.text: They may bar access, threatening deliveries

definitions.meaning: door staff at a nightclub who turn people away
in cricket, short-pitched balls that rear up at the batsman

explanation.surface: Something keeps people out with intimidating parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's delivery that rears up at the batter's head shares its name with nightclub door staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Door staff at clubs stop entry; short fast balls in cricket menace the batter.

clue.text: Expression of appreciation replacing love in marriage? That's a rare thing

indicators.note: replacing says one piece takes the place of another inside the word

parts.note: a union is a marriage
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O
cor is a British exclamation of admiration or surprise

explanation.surface: A word of thanks is offered instead of affection in a marriage, which is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of wonder. 'replacing' swaps the O of UNION for COR.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical horned horse is a byword for something seldom or never found.

clue.text: Team held back practical inventor

indicators.note: held back means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a side is a team
on means feasible, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A team was restrained by a down-to-earth inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reverses SIDE to EDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Central staff provide gloss on message: "Nothing cut from benefit"

parts.note: to spin is to present news in a flattering light

indicators.note: cut from means a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Head-office employees put a positive spin on a message about benefit cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central staff' looks like headquarters personnel, but means a rod at the centre. 'cut from' removes O from DOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a rod or axis around which something turns.

clue.text: Italy: singer from there mostly a would-be high-flier

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian tenor

explanation.surface: An Italian singer is mostly an aspiring star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CARUSO to CARUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he flew on wax wings too near the sun and fell.

clue.text: Stars working to enthral Olympic city

indicators.note: to enthral means to captivate, holding the other piece inside

parts.note: on means operating or working
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games

explanation.surface: Celebrities are busy charming an Olympic host city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enthral' is the container signal; 'Stars' looks like celebrities but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter constellation is a group of bright stars.

clue.text: Obligation is deemed to be withdrawn, limiting college treasury heartlessly

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, keeping the other piece within bounds
withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: is seen means is considered or deemed

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle is removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A duty is said to be withdrawn, capping a college's funds without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reverses IS SEEN to NEESSI; 'limiting' puts C inside it; 'heartlessly' keeps TY from treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one must do is a requirement or necessary duty.

clue.text: Greek character upset British author touring capital of Greece

indicators.note: touring means going round, enclosing the other piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, reversed

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A troubled English writer travels around Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses AMIS to SIMA; 'touring' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to S.

clue.text: Digger, almost new, acquired by one working around house?

indicators.note: acquired by says the trimmed word is taken inside the other

parts.note: an ironer presses clothes as a domestic chore

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: mint means brand new, as in mint condition

explanation.surface: A nearly new excavator is bought by a home help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' and 'acquired by' are the indicators; 'Digger' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who excavates ore underground is a miner, a kind of digger.

clue.text: Wild year, chasing daughters in pursuit of soldier

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so this piece comes after
chasing means coming after, so this piece follows

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A frenzied year spent chasing girls who are chasing a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dizzy with excitement or frivolously excitable is being wild.

clue.text: Certainly squeals when recording is taken away

indicators.note: is taken away means removed from the longer word

parts.note: yelps are sharp cries
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone surely shrieks when a record is confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken away' removes LP from YELPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative reply such as of course means agreement, certainly.

clue.text: Rev, good Unitarian on the outside

definitions.note: to rev an engine is to open the throttle, the verb sense

indicators.note: on the outside means only the outermost letters are used

explanation.surface: A clergyman is a decent Unitarian, at least outwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a cleric, but is the verb meaning to race an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To open the throttle on a motor is to race or accelerate it hard.

clue.text: They provide gear mother, heading for kitchen, used to fill sideboards

indicators.note: used to fill says these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: dressers are kitchen sideboards with shelves
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter only

explanation.surface: Mother takes kitchen things to stock the dressers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to fill' puts MAK inside DRESSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Garment makers produce clothing, which is gear in the sense of outfits.
